handoff: Changes requested, 2 blocking: AC1's Codex/Gemini half is unproven (no adapter test asserts SessionStart source reaches message); the attended-step note offers norn ask, which the brief forbids. Minor: no guard after a standing report, duplicated reminder wording, stale summary.

findings.title: Codex's and Gemini's session sources are not proven to reach the note
findings.detail:
AC1: "when a session starts from compact, resume or clear (Claude's sources and Codex's and Gemini's equivalents)". The core test "Codex's and Gemini's session starts from resume or clear are re-oriented the same way" only changes `fact.agent`, and hookAnswer never reads that field, so it shows nothing about either tool. Whether the note appears depends on each adapter putting the native `source` into HookFact.message (packages/adapters/src/codex/index.ts:45, gemini/index.ts:50). No test asserts this. codex.test.ts:18 matches SessionStart without `message`, and gemini.test.ts has no parse case for SessionStart. Only Claude pins it (claude.test.ts). If that mapping regressed, no test would catch it.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add parse cases in codex.test.ts and gemini.test.ts that assert a resume (and, for Gemini, a clear) SessionStart payload yields `message: "resume"`/`"clear"`, from the recorded fixtures.

findings.title: The session-start note at an attended step tells the agent to use `norn ask`
findings.detail:
sessionNote uses reportLine(step) for every agent step. That line always ends with "`norn ask "<question>"` or `norn stuck …`". At an attended step, the brief says "ask them in this session; never `norn ask`" (packages/core/src/brief.ts:753, and the Where you run line at :780). attendedReminder (hook.ts:92) says "ask in this session rather than with `norn ask`" in the same session. So after a compact, an attended agent gets two contradictory instructions. The unit test "an attended step is re-oriented too" (packages/core/test/unit/hook-answer.test.ts) checks only the step name, so it misses this. D10 asks for "its reportable outcomes", and `norn ask` is not an outcome the person wants used at an attended step.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: At an attended step, leave `norn ask` out of the note's report line, or replace it with the attended wording the brief uses. Extend "an attended step is re-oriented too" to assert that the note does not offer `norn ask`.

findings.title: The note and the reminder ignore a standing report and a parked step
findings.detail:
turnEndBlock (hook.ts:46-50) checks the status (running/ready), that the session is not foreign, and that no report is standing. sessionNote and attendedReminder check none of these. A session compacted after `norn done`, or while it is parked on `norn ask`, is still told "Report exactly once". A second report is refused, so the harm is a wasted turn. D10 asks only for a loadable state at an agent step, so this is a refinement, not a criterion miss.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Use the same status and standingReport guards as turnEndBlock, or word the note so it holds once the step has reported.

findings.title: The reminder restates the brief's attended line in its own words; the hook command's summary is stale
findings.detail:
The reminder hard-codes "`norn done`"/"`norn ask`" and its own wording, instead of using cmd.* and a text shared with brief.ts:780. The two can drift apart. packages/cli/src/commands/hook.ts:111 still has the summary "record a lifecycle fact; refuse an unreported turn end", but the command now also adds context.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Share one constant between the brief and the reminder. Update the summary and run docs:emit.

findings.title: Neither Codex nor Gemini fires SessionStart on compaction
findings.detail:
Per their hook docs, Gemini's SessionStart source is startup|resume|clear, and compaction fires PreCompress, which is not installed or mapped. Codex's source is startup|resume. So after compaction those tools get no note. Every non-startup source is handled, and the spec's Risks already say these encodings are unobserved. This is a gap to record, not a miswired value.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Record it under the handoff's Not proven yet. Mapping Gemini's PreCompress or an after-compact event is later work.

findings.title: The note test takes its expected rules from the same list the code uses
findings.detail:
`for (const r of HARD_RULES) expect(text).toContain(ruleWithReason(r.id))` proves every rule is present, but not its wording. That matches the slice's one-source note, and the brief's snapshot pins the wording, so this is not rework.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optionally pin one rule's literal text.
